result.summary: Transaction lookup routines in node::GetTransaction and TxIndex::FindTx/FindLegacyTx are updated to throw std::runtime_error on disk I/O, deserialization, and index corruption failures rather than returning null. ProcessPSBT is refactored to reuse GetTransaction instead of doing duplicate lookups. Additionally, getrawtransaction with an explicit block hash now invokes CheckBlockDataAvailability to distinguish pruned or not-yet-downloaded blocks from missing transactions.
result.problem: When disk reads or index lookups fail due to file I/O or corrupt index entries, transaction retrieval returns null or nullopt, which callers interpret as a non-existent transaction. As a result, confirmed transactions appear missing and underlying disk failures or index corruptions go undetected by RPC clients and node operators.
evidence: Commit e0b20465bb: 'Currently the GetTransaction return value is a nullable transaction pointer, where nullptr represents two different outcomes: I/O error and missing tx. Reporting a confirmed transaction as missing is wrong, so properly return an error instead.'
Commit e0b20465bb: '...a -txindex corruption may also point to a larger system corruption and it seems better to notify the user properly by throwing an exception.'
result.changed_since_previous: The overall approach and scope remain the same; changes from the prior version are limited to rebase adjustments across the commits.
result.card: This PR causes node::GetTransaction and TxIndex lookup functions to throw runtime errors on file I/O, deserialization failures, and index corruption instead of returning null pointers. Today, disk and index read errors are indistinguishable from missing transactions, masking disk or database corruption from RPC users and services. It also updates getrawtransaction with a block hash to return clear availability errors for pruned or un-downloaded blocks, and refactors ProcessPSBT to use GetTransaction.

risk.why: Throwing runtime exceptions on previously silent disk read failures changes RPC error behavior and error codes when disk I/O fails.
